NetworkKey.description: The set of properties present depends on the key's type - every type is now documented: WPA1/WPA2 (WPA-PSK), WPA3, WPA3_OWE, WPA_EAP (all 7 eapMethod variants), WPA_EAP_SCEP, IEEE_802_1X (all 5 eapMethod variants), OPEN_HTTP, HTTP_AUTHENTICATION, and RAW.

subKeyId.description: id of an existing HTTP_AUTHENTICATION network key this one references, if any. Applies to WPA1/WPA2, WPA3, WPA3_OWE, WPA_EAP (all 7 eapMethod variants), WPA_EAP_SCEP, and RAW. Not applicable to IEEE_802_1X, OPEN_HTTP, or HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - none of those have a subKeyId concept.

keyFileContent.description: RAW only - a raw wpa_supplicant.conf-style config block. "" when not configured, never null. Note there's no separate ssid/bssid field even though the domain model has them - a raw config embeds the actual SSID/BSSID inline as placeholders within this text itself (e.g. "ssid=__SSID__"), so the separate fields would be redundant.

usePassphrase.description: WPA1/WPA2 only - true if passphraseOrPsk is a passphrase, false if it's a raw hex PSK. WPA3 has no equivalent - it's always passphrase-based (see 'pure' instead).

pure.description: WPA3 only - true for "WPA3 only" mode, false for "Mixed WPA3/WPA2-PSK" mode

passphraseOrPsk.description: WPA1/WPA2/WPA3 only - masked to "********" when set; the actual passphrase/PSK is never returned. WPA3_OWE has no shared secret at all, so this is absent for it.

eapMethod.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X - determines which of the eapMethod-specific fields below are meaningful (IEEE_802_1X only supports 5 of the 7 values - no EAP_PSK/EAP_FAST)

wpaVersion.description: WPA_EAP and WPA_EAP_SCEP only - the WPA generation this EAP key is used with. IEEE_802_1X has no version concept at all.

identity.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, all eapMethod variants of either

allowAny.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, all eapMethod variants of either - Configurator's "Allow any" option

caCertificate.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X (eapMethod EAP_TTLS or EAP_MSCHAP_V2 of either), WPA_EAP_SCEP, OPEN_HTTP, and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - public cert, not a secret. EAP_PEAP has its own separate caCertificate field below at the same level (Configurator only enables a CA certificate for PEAP, not client cert/private key).

authenticationUrl.description: OPEN_HTTP only - the URL the Eye authenticates against

requireServerCertificateCheck.description: OPEN_HTTP and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - gates the whole certificate block: when false, caCertificate/clientCertificate/privateKey are never populated even if previously set. This is the inverse of the domain model's own "no server certificate check" flag.

postData.description: OPEN_HTTP only - the HTTP POST body sent to authenticationUrl; "" when not configured, never null

clientCertificateFileType.description: OPEN_HTTP and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - only present alongside an actual clientCertificate; a file type is meaningless without a certificate for it to describe

privateKeyFileType.description: OPEN_HTTP and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - only present alongside an actual privateKeyFileName, same reasoning as clientCertificateFileType

targetUrl.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - the URL the Eye authenticates against

contentOnTargetUrlPage.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - expected content on the target URL's page, used to detect whether login is already satisfied

contentOnLoginPage.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - expected content on the login page

contentOnSuccessfulLogin.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - expected content after a successful login

contentOnUnSuccessfulLogin.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - expected content after a failed login

userAgent.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - one of Configurator's ~100 named user agent strings (e.g. "WINDOWS7_FIREFOX", its own default), or "CUSTOM_USER_AGENT" to use customUserAgent instead

customUserAgent.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - only present when userAgent is CUSTOM_USER_AGENT; meaningless (and absent) for every other userAgent value

loginPages.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - an ordered list of login pages, each a set of form fields. Omitted entirely (not an empty array) when there are none.

logoutPages.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - same shape as loginPages, for the logout sequence

scepUrl.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - the SCEP server URL the Eye enrolls its client certificate against

challengePassword.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - masked to "********" when set; the actual password is never returned

subjectName.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - the certificate subject name (DN) to request

keySize.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - RSA key size for the generated keypair

renewalThresholdPercent.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - percentage of the certificate's validity period elapsed before the Eye renews it

clientCertificate.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X (eapMethod EAP_TTLS or EAP_MSCHAP_V2 of either), OPEN_HTTP, and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - public cert, not a secret. Always present for IEEE_802_1X's EAP_TTLS specifically - Configurator requires it there, unlike WPA_EAP's EAP_TTLS where it's optional.

privateKeyFileName.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X (eapMethod EAP_TLS of either), OPEN_HTTP, and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - filename only, never the key bytes themselves

privateKeyPassword.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_TLS of either - masked to "********" when set; the actual password is never returned

peapLabel.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_PEAP of either

peapVersion.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_PEAP of either

innerAuthenticationMethod.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_PEAP of either - the PEAP "Inner Authentication" method

ttlsInnerAuthenticationMethod.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_TTLS of either - the TTLS "Inner Authentication" method (a separate, larger enum than PEAP's own)

preSharedKey.description: WPA_EAP only, eapMethod EAP_PSK - masked to "********" when set; the actual key is never returned

pacFileName.description: WPA_EAP only, eapMethod EAP_FAST - filename only, the PAC file's bytes are never returned

anonymousIdentity.description: WPA_EAP, eapMethod EAP_TTLS or EAP_FAST; or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_TTLS (IEEE_802_1X has no EAP_FAST)

password.description: WPA_EAP, eapMethod EAP_PEAP, EAP_TTLS, EAP_FAST, LEAP, or EAP_MSCHAP_V2; or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_PEAP, EAP_TTLS, LEAP, or EAP_MSCHAP_V2 (IEEE_802_1X has no EAP_FAST) - the outer EAP password, masked to "********" when set; the actual password is never returned

innerCaCertificate.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_PEAP or EAP_TTLS of either with their inner method set to TLS/EAP_TLS - public cert, not a secret

innerClientCertificate.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_PEAP or EAP_TTLS of either with their inner method set to TLS/EAP_TLS - public cert, not a secret

innerPrivateKeyFileName.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_PEAP or EAP_TTLS of either with their inner method set to TLS/EAP_TLS - filename only

innerPrivateKeyPassword.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, eapMethod EAP_PEAP or EAP_TTLS of either with their inner method set to TLS/EAP_TLS - masked to "********" when set

NetworkKeyType.description: Determines which other fields are meaningful on a NetworkKey/NetworkKeyRequest. Every value is now documented with request/response fields and examples.

EapMethod.description: Determines which WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X request shape applies - see the request examples for each. IEEE_802_1X only supports 5 of these 7 values - EAP_PSK and EAP_FAST are WPA_EAP only.

CertificateType.description: OPEN_HTTP and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - PEM vs DER for clientCertificate/privateKey. Required whenever the corresponding certificate is provided; there's no safe default since it's a fact about the uploaded bytes, not a preference.

SecureProtocol.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - optional, defaults to AUTOMATIC when omitted

ScepKeySize.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - RSA key size for the Eye-generated keypair. Optional, defaults to RSA_2048 when omitted.

WpaVersion.description: The WPA generation a WPA_EAP key is used with - distinct from the top-level 'type' WPA1/WPA2/WPA3 values, which instead select a WPA-PSK request shape.

PEAPLabel.description: EAP_PEAP only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - optional, defaults to CLIENT_EAP_ENCRYPTION when omitted

PEAPVersion.description: EAP_PEAP only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - optional, defaults to V0 when omitted

PEAPInnerAuthenticationMethod.description: EAP_PEAP only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - the caCertificate/clientCertificate/privateKey/privateKeyPassword fields on PeapInnerAuthentication only apply when this is TLS

InnerAuthenticationMethod.description: EAP_TTLS only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - a separate, larger enum than PEAP's own PEAPInnerAuthenticationMethod. The caCertificate/clientCertificate/privateKey/privateKeyPassword fields on TtlsInnerAuthentication only apply when this is EAP_TLS

TlsVersion.description: EAP_FAST only - optional, defaults to TLS_1_0 when omitted or explicitly ANY

CertificateFile.description: A certificate/private-key/PAC file. certificateBytes is the raw file content, base64-encoded.

HttpAuthenticationPage.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - one step in a multi-step login/logout sequence. Configurator's own UI keys pages by a page number, but that number is purely a transient UI grouping aid never actually persisted - only the resulting order survives, which is why this shape is just a plain ordered list of pages with no page-number field.

CertificateProperties.description: EAP_TLS only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - the outer "Certificate Properties" panel. All fields optional; omitting the whole object, or any certificate within it, on update leaves it untouched rather than clearing it.

PeapInnerAuthentication.description: EAP_PEAP only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - the "Inner Authentication" panel. caCertificate/clientCertificate/privateKey/privateKeyPassword only apply when method is TLS; clientCertificate is required in that case.

TtlsInnerAuthentication.description: EAP_TTLS only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - the "Inner Authentication" panel. caCertificate/clientCertificate/privateKey/privateKeyPassword only apply when method is EAP_TLS; clientCertificate is required in that case.

PostNetworkKeyRequest.description: Request shape is resolved from 'type' (and, for WPA_EAP/IEEE_802_1X, further resolved from 'eapMethod') - see their own descriptions for which values are documented. WPA_EAP_SCEP, OPEN_HTTP, and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION are top-level shapes in their own right, with no 'eapMethod'. See the request examples for concrete payloads.

usePassphrase.description: WPA1/WPA2 only - required for those types. WPA3 has no equivalent - it's always passphrase-based (see 'pure' instead). Not applicable to WPA3_OWE or WPA_EAP.

pure.description: WPA3 only - required for that type. true for "WPA3 only" mode, false for "Mixed WPA3/WPA2-PSK" mode. Not applicable to any other type.

passphraseOrPsk.description: WPA1/WPA2/WPA3 only - required for those types. Not applicable to WPA3_OWE, which has no shared secret at all, or WPA_EAP.

subKeyId.description: id of an existing HTTP_AUTHENTICATION network key to reference, if any. Applies to WPA1/WPA2/WPA3/WPA3_OWE, WPA_EAP (all 7 eapMethod variants), WPA_EAP_SCEP, and RAW below. Not applicable to IEEE_802_1X, OPEN_HTTP, or HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - none of those have a subKeyId concept.

eapMethod.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X - required for those types; resolves which of the eapMethod-specific fields below apply. IEEE_802_1X only supports 5 of the 7 values (no EAP_PSK/EAP_FAST). See the request examples.

wpaVersion.description: WPA_EAP (all eapMethod variants) and WPA_EAP_SCEP - required for both. Not applicable to IEEE_802_1X, which has no version concept at all.

identity.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, all eapMethod variants of either - required

allowAny.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X, all eapMethod variants of either - required

eapolVersion.description: WPA_EAP (all eapMethod variants) and WPA_EAP_SCEP - optional for both

certificateProperties.description: EAP_TLS only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - optional as a whole, and every field within it is optional too

scepUrl.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - required, must start with "http://" or "https://"

subjectName.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - required, the certificate subject name (DN) to request

keySize.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - optional, defaults to RSA_2048

renewalThresholdPercent.description: WPA_EAP_SCEP only - optional, defaults to 33, must be between 1 and 99

password.description: Required for WPA_EAP's EAP_PEAP, EAP_TTLS, EAP_FAST, LEAP, and EAP_MSCHAP_V2, and for IEEE_802_1X's EAP_PEAP, EAP_TTLS, LEAP, and EAP_MSCHAP_V2 (IEEE_802_1X has no EAP_FAST) - the outer EAP password. Not applicable to EAP_TLS or EAP_PSK.

peapLabel.description: EAP_PEAP only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - optional, defaults to CLIENT_EAP_ENCRYPTION

peapVersion.description: EAP_PEAP only (WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X) - optional, defaults to V0

caCertificate.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X - optional for eapMethod EAP_TTLS or EAP_MSCHAP_V2 of either (EAP_PEAP also has a caCertificate at this same level - its outer "Certificate Properties" only enables the CA certificate field). WPA_EAP_SCEP, OPEN_HTTP, and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - also optional; omitting it (or any certificate field) on update leaves whatever was previously stored untouched rather than clearing it - there is currently no way to clear a certificate once set. For OPEN_HTTP/HTTP_AUTHENTICATION specifically, the whole certificate block (caCertificate/clientCertificate/privateKey) is also gated by requireServerCertificateCheck - when that's false, these fields are ignored entirely even if supplied.

innerAuthentication.description: WPA_EAP or IEEE_802_1X - shape depends on eapMethod: PeapInnerAuthentication for EAP_PEAP, TtlsInnerAuthentication for EAP_TTLS. See the request examples.

anonymousIdentity.description: Required for WPA_EAP's EAP_TTLS and EAP_FAST, and for IEEE_802_1X's EAP_TTLS (IEEE_802_1X has no EAP_FAST)

clientCertificate.description: WPA_EAP - optional for eapMethod EAP_TTLS or EAP_MSCHAP_V2. IEEE_802_1X - optional for EAP_MSCHAP_V2, but REQUIRED for EAP_TTLS specifically (Configurator hard-errors if blank there, unlike WPA_EAP's EAP_TTLS where it's optional). OPEN_HTTP/HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - optional, but requires clientCertificateFileType whenever it's provided; gated by requireServerCertificateCheck (see caCertificate's own description).

clientCertificateFileType.description: OPEN_HTTP and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - required whenever clientCertificate is provided, since there's no safe PEM/DER default

privateKey.description: OPEN_HTTP and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - optional; requires privateKeyFileType whenever it's provided; gated by requireServerCertificateCheck (see caCertificate's own description)

privateKeyFileType.description: OPEN_HTTP and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - required whenever privateKey is provided, since there's no safe PEM/DER default

authenticationUrl.description: OPEN_HTTP only - required, the URL the Eye authenticates against

requireServerCertificateCheck.description: OPEN_HTTP and HTTP_AUTHENTICATION - required for both. A single flag that both controls whether the server's certificate is verified AND gates whether caCertificate/clientCertificate/privateKey are processed at all - matching Configurator's own single checkbox for this. This is the inverse of the domain model's own "no server certificate check" flag.

postData.description: OPEN_HTTP only - optional; omitting it stores an empty string, matching Configurator's own behavior when its "use HTTP POST" checkbox is unchecked

targetUrl.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - required, the URL the Eye authenticates against

secureProtocol.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - optional, defaults to AUTOMATIC when omitted

userAgent.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - optional, defaults to "WINDOWS7_FIREFOX" when omitted. One of Configurator's ~100 named user agent strings, or "CUSTOM_USER_AGENT" to use customUserAgent instead.

customUserAgent.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - only meaningful when userAgent is CUSTOM_USER_AGENT; Configurator forces it to "" for every other userAgent value, and this request does the same rather than erroring if it's supplied anyway

loginPages.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - an ordered list of login pages, each a set of form fields. Omitting this field on update leaves whatever was previously stored untouched; sending an explicit empty array clears it (the one certificate-like field on this template that CAN be cleared, since an empty array is distinguishable from an omitted field).

logoutPages.description: HTTP_AUTHENTICATION only - same shape and update/clear semantics as loginPages, for the logout sequence

keyFileContent.description: RAW only - optional; omitting it stores an empty string. A raw wpa_supplicant.conf-style config block - there's no separate ssid/bssid field even though the domain model has them, since a raw config embeds the actual SSID/BSSID inline as placeholders within this text itself (e.g. "ssid=__SSID__").

preSharedKey.description: WPA_EAP EAP_PSK only - required, exactly 32 hex characters (a 128-bit key, not a passphrase)

tlsVersion.description: WPA_EAP EAP_FAST only - optional, defaults to TLS_1_0 when omitted or explicitly ANY

pacFile.description: WPA_EAP EAP_FAST only - required, unlike every other EAP method's certificate fields
